coverage_notes: Zero-day versus known vulnerability: the boundary is drawn from ENISA's words. TR49: 'unknown to the user', 'unknown unknown', 'compared to regular software exploits'. TR48: weaknesses from 'poor configuration and/or logic or implementation erros'. SPARTA's EX-0009.03 is defined on 'publicly or privately known defects' (TR48 only); RD-0003.01 mentions 0-day packages (TR49 only); the unqualified EX-0009 is shared by both.
The user_terminal vector is removed: its chain stopped at the hosted RAN function and gave no scenario result.

TR49 and TR48 share the same exploit step EX-0009 and the rf_link/ground entries. TR49 differs from TR48 by the 0-day acquisition step RD-0003.01 and by keeping no flaw-class child (EX-0009.01/.02/.03), because SPARTA has no zero-day flag and ENISA names no class; TR48 adds the known-defect preparation REC-0008.03.
